name: dfa_bottom50_shares
title: The bottom half by wealth owes half the consumer credit and a fifth of mortgages
source_line: Source: Fed Distributional Financial Accounts, dfa-networth-shares.csv (vintage DFA 2026-09-15 (through 2026Q2)); chart: household-debt-risk
units: Bottom 50% by wealth: percent of aggregate (%)
alt_text: Line chart titled "The bottom half by wealth owes half the consumer credit and a fifth of mortgages": Home mortgages, Consumer credit, Net worth (Bottom 50% by wealth: percent of aggregate (%)) by quarter, 1989Q3 to 2026Q2, 148 observations. Home mortgages fell from 27.5% in 1989Q3 to 22.6% in 2026Q2 (high 34.6% in 2010Q3; low 22.1% in 2021Q1). Consumer credit rose from 43.8% in 1989Q3 to 51.6% in 2026Q2 (high 58.1% in 2013Q1). Net worth fell from 3.50% in 1989Q3 to 2.30% in 2026Q2 (high 4.10% in 1992Q3; low 0.40% in 2010Q4). Shaded bands mark 4 NBER recessions (1990Q3 to 2020Q2).
